title: Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change the funding, marketing and governance arrangements for rural research and development corporations, including statutory corporations and organisations owned by industry.

It would permit industry-requested marketing by statutory corporations and government matching of voluntary research contributions, subject to existing caps and excluding marketing from matching funding.
The package sits alongside companion customs charge and excise levy bills, and would introduce published funding agreements for statutory corporations covering expenditure conditions.
changes: Director selection committees would have at most five members and could operate for up to three years.
Lists of suitable candidates could be used to fill vacancies over the following 12 months.
Separately levied fisheries could receive matching funding capped by their own gross value of production.
Statutory corporations would no longer need ministerial approval for annual operating plans.
summary.affected: Rural research and development corporations, levy-paying industries, voluntary research contributors and separately levied fisheries are affected.

speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of a companion bill removing maximum research, development and marketing levy rate caps from the Primary Industries (Excise) Levies Act 1999, requiring any levy rate to be recommended by industry bodies after consulting levy payers.

speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of a further companion bill removing maximum research, development and marketing charge rate caps from the Primary Industries (Customs) Charges Act 1999, on the same basis as the companion levies bill.

speeches.speaker: John Cobb
speeches.brief: Supported the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill allowing all 15 research and development corporations to undertake marketing activities where industry requests it, noting nine are already industry-owned, but criticised the government for giving industry only a little over a week to review the changes before passage.

speeches.speaker: Dick Adams
speeches.brief: Detailed the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill's changes across 10 acts affecting 15 research and development corporations, including new funding agreements required from July 2014 and streamlined board selection processes, and paid tribute to retiring committee colleague Alby Schultz.

speeches.speaker: Sharman Stone
speeches.brief: Supported the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill but argued New Zealand should contribute to Australian RDC marketing levies under the Closer Economic Relations agreement since its exporters benefit too, and lamented that the Tatura Research Institute, once a world leader in orchard trellis systems, now has virtually no research scientists left.

speeches.speaker: Sid Sidebottom
speeches.brief: Summed up the debate, defending the government's three years of consultation on the rural research and development changes, noting the exposure draft had been offered to 72 stakeholders with only seven replying, most of them positive.

speeches.speaker: Kate Lundy
speeches.brief: The Grape and Wine Legislation Amendment Bill creates the Australian Grape and Wine Authority from 1 July 2014, merging the Grape and Wine Research and Development Corporation and Wine Australia Corporation to improve industry efficiency, while the Rural Research and Development Legislation Amendment Bill allows statutory research and development corporations to undertake marketing and match voluntary contributions. The Homelessness Bill sets a target to halve homelessness by 2020 and provide supported accommodation for all rough sleepers, with a revised definition recognising those in crisis accommodation or unsafe homes.
